subject: Numeracy
title: Number games
objectives: Children will play games that practise counting and numerals to 10.
Children will show how many in a group with fingers or objects.
content: Number hop and jump, number hunt, and counting bags.
teachingActivities: Use games to practise rather than teach new ideas; keep rules simple; let children play in pairs; watch for children who guess and not count; note children who need more practice.
learnerActivities: Play counting games with confidence and count out a number of objects when asked.
assessment: Observe whether each child counts out a number of objects when asked and plays games with confidence.
expectedOutcomes: Counts out a number of objects when asked.

lessons.title: Number hopscotch
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will hop along a number grid and say each number.
successCriteria: Hops on numbers 1 to 10 in order
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10, count objects and name numerals 1 to 10.
resources: A chalk or tape hopscotch grid
lessons.starter: Show a number grid and say "Let us play hopscotch and count as we hop."
teacherActivities: Show how to hop from one number to the next.
Let children take turns to hop and count.
Throw a beanbag on a number and say it.
Cheer for every child who counts.
learnerActivities: Child hops and says each number.
Child throws and names the number.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hop from one number to the next. Children: Children watch and count.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children take turns to hop and count. Children: Child hops and says each number.
Step 3. Teacher: Throw a beanbag on a number and say it. Children: Child throws and names the number.
Step 4. Teacher: Cheer for every child who counts. Children: Children clap and cheer.

practical.title: Hopscotch
practical.safety: Use a flat non-slip surface and supervise every hop. Keep beanbag throwing gentle and away from faces.

differentiation.support: Walk the grid holding hands and say the numbers.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to hop in twos.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What number did your beanbag land on?

lessons.conclusion: Count the beanbags back into a basket.
lessons.homeConnection: Draw a hopscotch grid with chalk and play together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hop along a number grid and say each number" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Number hunt
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find numerals hidden around the room and say them.
successCriteria: Names the numeral and counts that many
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10, count objects and name numerals 1 to 10.
lessons.starter: Say "I have hidden numbers around the room. Can you find them?"
teacherActivities: Show a sample card and explain the game.
Let children hunt for numeral cards.
Ask each child to say the numeral and count out that many counters.
Put the numerals in order together.
learnerActivities: Child names the numeral and counts.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a sample card and explain the game. Children: Children look and nod.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children hunt for numeral cards. Children: Child finds a numeral card.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask each child to say the numeral and count out that many counters. Children: Child names the numeral and counts.
Step 4. Teacher: Put the numerals in order together. Children: Children place cards in order.

practical.title: Numeral hunt
practical.safety: Hide cards at child height away from hazards and supervise the hunt. Keep the room tidy.

differentiation.support: Hunt in a small area with the child and find numerals 1 to 5.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a numeral and write it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the numerals in order and say them aloud.
lessons.homeConnection: Hide numeral cards at home and hunt for them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find numerals hidden around the room and say them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting bags
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will fill a bag with the number of objects on a card.
successCriteria: Counts the right number into a bag
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10, count objects and name numerals 1 to 10.
lessons.starter: Show a bag labelled 6 and say "Put six counters inside this bag."
teacherActivities: Show how to count six into a bag.
Let each child fill a bag to match the label.
Tip out the bag and check.
Swap bags with a friend and check.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to count six into a bag. Children: Children watch and count.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child fill a bag to match the label. Children: Child counts into a bag.
Step 3. Teacher: Tip out the bag and check. Children: Child counts again to check.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap bags with a friend and check. Children: Child checks a friend’s bag.

practical.title: Fill the bag
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise tipping. Keep bags away from faces.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a bag labelled 12.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many are in the bag?

expectedOutcomes: Counts the right number into a bag
lessons.conclusion: Put the bags away and say the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Fill a small bag with the number of objects on a card.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "fill a bag with the number of objects on a card" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Show me with fingers
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show numbers to ten with their fingers.
successCriteria: Shows a number to 10 with fingers
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10, count objects and name numerals 1 to 10.
lessons.starter: Hold up a numeral card and say "Show me with your fingers."
teacherActivities: Show the numeral 3 and make three with fingers.
Call out numbers and let children show them.
Use two hands to show numbers over five.
learnerActivities: Children show the number with fingers.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the numeral 3 and make three with fingers. Children: Children copy with their fingers.
Step 2. Teacher: Call out numbers and let children show them. Children: Children show the number with fingers.
Step 3. Teacher: Use two hands to show numbers over five. Children: Child shows six to ten.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many fingers?" Children: Child says the number.

practical.title: Fingers game
practical.safety: Keep the game seated and gentle so that no child is hit. Accept different finger patterns for the same number.

differentiation.support: Show the finger pattern beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to show a number in two different ways.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put your hands in your lap and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Show numbers with fingers while counting at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show numbers to ten with their fingers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 number games check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how confidently each child plays counting games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 10, count objects and name numerals 1 to 10.
lessons.starter: Sing the number song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: hopscotch, counting bags and numeral hunt.
At each station watch how the child counts.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: hopscotch, counting bags and numeral hunt. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child counts. Children: Child counts with confidence.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Game stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use large counters only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use numbers up to five.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to lead a game.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: counts out a number; names numerals; plays counting games; takes turns.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep playing number games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how confidently each child plays counting games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
